lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Horoscopes for Other Universes. The stars are different there. So are you.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: This is Madame Orrery. I have never been wrong, in any universe I've checked.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Horoscopes for Other Universes, on ninety five point six five. Your future, slightly to the left.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Horoscopes for Other Universes. Whatever you were born under, dear, you're welcome here.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Good morning. This is The Morning Alignment. The stars are where I left them. A good start.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: A quick planetary update before your coffee. Mercury is in a mood. Not retrograde. Just a mood.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Give it some space, and don't send any important letters. Or do. Mercury can't stop you, dear. It's very far away, and sulking.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Welcome to Compatibility Hour. Tell me your sign, and theirs, and which universe they're from. Nothing surprises the stars. They're very far away.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Compatibility Hour. Hello, dear.

lines.speaker: Caller, a Teapot
lines.text: Hi, Madame Orrery. I'm a Teapot, and I've met someone lovely. But she's a Ladder.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Oh, that's a beautiful match. A Teapot and a Ladder. That's a cup of tea, on a high shelf.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Someone has to climb up for it. Someone has to be worth climbing for.

lines.speaker: Caller, a Teapot
lines.text: Which one of us is which?

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: You take turns, dear. That's the whole secret. That's every secret, really.

lines.speaker: Caller, a Single Sock
lines.text: Hello? I'm a Single Sock. I've been told the other sock is in another universe.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: It is, dear. I've seen it. It's under a radiator, in a universe very like this one. It's warm. It's thinking of you.

lines.speaker: Caller, a Single Sock
lines.text: Should I go and get it?

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: No. Wear odd socks. It's how the multiverse knows you're keeping a place for someone.

lines.speaker: Caller, a Single Sock
lines.text: Oh. Oh, that's nice.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Charts for the Night Shift. For everyone working while the sky does the rest.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: For the operator on the relay ship tonight. I did your chart, dear.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: You were born under a star you can't see from where you are. That's all right. It can see you. It says: drink the tea while it's hot.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: A reading for the bakers, who are up now, and the night nurses, and the man who drives the empty bus. Your sign tonight is The Lamp Left On.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Somebody is getting home safely because of you. They'll never know your name. The stars do.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The Teapot. Steady, warm, and best left alone for four minutes.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The Ladder. You were born on the way up, and you've never fully settled. Hold on with both hands, dear.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The Single Sock. Born alone, in a drawer, quite sure there was another one of you somewhere. There is. Listen.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The Blinking Cat. The only constellation that looks back. Unbothered, and right about most things.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The Spare Key. Born under a flowerpot, just in case. People rely on you more than they say.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The Paper Boat. Born in a puddle after rain. Brave, light, and slightly damp.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: This week, a door you've been pushing will turn out to be a pull. Don't be embarrassed, dear. The door has been waiting for you to notice, and it's very pleased that you did.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Venus enters your fourth house. Not the Venus you're thinking of. Your universe's Venus, which is a sort of shed at the bottom of a garden.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Something in the shed wants to be found. Probably a bicycle pump. Go and look anyway.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Someone will say your name in a supermarket, and it won't be for you. Turn around anyway. It's good for the neck, and you'll see something you needed to see.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Probably the biscuits.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The stars suggest a conversation with a relative. I've checked, and yes, dear, it's that one. It goes much better than you expect. They've been rehearsing too.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Money. A coin you lost in another universe will turn up in this one, under a sofa, slightly warmer than it ought to be.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Spend it on something small and pointless. That's what it wants.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Love. Someone across the multiverse is thinking about you right now. They are also thinking about lunch.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Don't take it personally. It's a very big multiverse, and it's nearly lunchtime in most of it.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Health. Drink more water. I know. Everyone says it. But I'm saying it from a universe where water is rarer than gold, and here you are, with a tap.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Have a glass, dear. Have one for us.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Your ruling planet moves into the house of small mercies. Expect a lift that arrives just as you press the button, and a parking space you'll tell people about for years.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Your lucky number is eleven and a half. Your lucky colour is the green of a traffic light, just before it changes.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Lucky item: a spoon you've never used. Lucky day: the second Tuesday, if it comes.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Your lucky direction is slightly to the left. Your lucky smell is toast. Avoid geese until Thursday.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Lucky number: four hundred and nine. Lucky stone: the one in your shoe. Take it out, dear. Luck isn't everything.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: My crystal ball is showing static again. It does that. It isn't broken.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: It's showing me the space between the stations, and that, dear, is where most of you are listening from.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: People ask how I can be so certain. I'm not certain, dear. I'm specific. It's much more useful.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The constellation shaped like a cat is blinking again. In the old charts, that means a visitor is coming.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: In the new charts, it means the cat is tired. I prefer the old charts.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: This week's planetary movements. Jupiter has moved, but not far. Saturn's rings are at the cleaners and should be back by Friday.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: A minor comet will pass very close to your house on Thursday evening. It isn't going to do anything. It's just looking. Wave, if you like.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: And the moon is full, in most universes. In one, it's only peckish.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: A special reading, for those born under The Lantern. It's a rare sign. It only rises once a year, when the veil between universes is at its thinnest.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Please don't lean on the veil, dear. It isn't load-bearing.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: This week, someone small will knock on your door and ask for sweets. Give them the good ones. In their universe, they're very important.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Lucky item: a torch. Lucky hour: just after dark. Lucky ghost: the polite one.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: A note for Halloween. This week, your sign is whatever you're dressed as. The stars respect a costume.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: If you've come as a sheet with two holes in it, your sign is The Laundry. You'll be fine, dear. You'll be folded by Sunday.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: A moon has gone missing, dear. Everyone agrees one's gone, and nobody agrees which.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: For The Ladder, it was yours. For The Teapot, it was someone else's. For everyone else, look under the bed. Moons get everywhere.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The whole of creation smells faintly of toast. I've checked the charts.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: A very good sign for The Teapot, and for anyone waiting for something to pop up. Have a slice, dear. The stars insist.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Everyone, under every sign, has the same song in their head tonight, and nobody can finish it.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: It's in the charts, dear. The ending rises next week, in the house of The Single Sock. Be patient.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: Three knocks at the planetarium door, dear. Nobody there.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: For The Spare Key, this is a sign. For everyone else, it's a door. Leave it be.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: The sky went a colour I've never seen, dear, and I've seen the sky in every universe I've checked.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: My crystal ball showed it for a moment. Then static again. Lucky colour: that one. Good luck finding it.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: A pigeon has walked into the back room, dear, and sat on the chart for The Paper Boat.

lines.speaker: Madame Orrery
lines.text: It knows people, I'm told. It certainly knows its sign. It's a Lamp Left On. You can always tell.
